name: Changsha
operatingHours: Changsha Metro runs ~6:30 AM–~11:00 PM daily (first and last trains vary by line and station; last trains from central stations leave ~10:30–11:00 PM). Trains every ~3–8 min by day, ~8–12 min late evening. No all-night service.
fareInfo: Distance-based single fares from ¥2 up to ~¥8 for the longest trips (2026). Pay with the Alipay or WeChat transit QR code (foreign Visa/Mastercard can be linked), with cash or mobile pay for a single-journey token at the machines, or with a transport card. 1-day (~¥15) and 3-day (~¥40) passes are sold. The airport Maglev Express is separate: ¥20 one way to Changsha South Station.

lines.name: Line 6
stations: Hunan University of Technology and Business

hotels.name: Days Hotel & Suites by Wyndham China Town Changsha
hotels.note: About a 15-minute walk west of the station along Wuyi Avenue (no other hotel meets our bar closer in).

sights.name: Hunan Museum
sights.note: The province's flagship museum, best known for the Mawangdui Han tombs: the 2,100-year-old preserved body of Lady Xin Zhui, lacquerware and silk paintings.
sights.hours: Tue–Sun ~9:00 AM–5:00 PM (last entry ~4:00 PM; longer hours in summer); closed Mondays. Free, but a real-name booking (passport) is required.

sights.name: Orange Isle (Juzizhou)
sights.note: A long, leafy island in the Xiang River with gardens, river views of the skyline and the huge Youth Mao Zedong head sculpture at its southern tip; Juzizhou metro station is on the island.
sights.hours: Open daily ~7:00 AM–10:00 PM; free (island tram extra). Fireworks on some holiday evenings.

sights.name: Mount Yuelu and Aiwan Pavilion
sights.note: A forested hill on the west bank with temple-dotted paths to the summit; the red Aiwan (Autumn-Admiring) Pavilion in the valley above Yuelu Academy is the classic spot for autumn leaves.
sights.hours: Scenic area open daily, roughly 6:00 AM–11:00 PM; free (cable car and shuttle bus extra).

sights.name: Yuelu Academy
sights.note: One of China's four great classical academies, founded in 976 and still part of Hunan University: quiet courtyards, lecture halls and a Confucian temple at the foot of Mount Yuelu.
sights.hours: Daily ~8:00 AM–5:30 PM (to ~6:00 PM in summer); ticket ~¥40.

sights.name: Changsha Museum
sights.note: The city museum in the riverside cultural complex on the north side, tracing Changsha from Neolithic finds and Chu bronzes to its revolutionary era.
sights.hours: Tue–Sun 9:00 AM–5:00 PM; closed Mondays; free (bring your passport).

sights.name: Hunan Martyrs' Park
sights.note: A large free park beside the Hunan Museum built around a lake, with a hilltop memorial tower, shady walks and locals dancing and exercising in the evenings.

sights.name: Kaifu Temple
sights.note: A working Buddhist temple founded over a thousand years ago, with incense-filled courtyards and a vegetarian restaurant, a few minutes' walk from Kaifu Temple metro station.
sights.hours: Daily ~8:00 AM–5:30 PM; small entry fee.

sights.name: Tianxin Pavilion
sights.note: A three-storey pavilion on the last surviving stretch of Changsha's Ming-dynasty city wall, set in a hillside park with views over the old town.
sights.hours: Park open daily; pavilion ~8:00 AM–5:30 PM, small ticket fee.

sights.name: Changsha Bamboo Slips Museum
sights.note: A compact, free museum built around the vast hoard of Three Kingdoms-era bamboo and wooden administrative slips found in wells under the city centre.
sights.hours: Tue–Sun 9:00 AM–5:00 PM; closed Mondays; free with passport.

sights.name: Huangxing Road Pedestrian Street
sights.note: Changsha's main car-free shopping street running south from the IFS towers, lined with chain stores, snack stands and bubble-tea queues; liveliest after dark.
sights.hours: Open all day; shops ~10:00 AM–10:00 PM.

sights.name: Taiping Street
sights.note: A restored lane of grey-brick shopfronts in the old quarter selling local snacks and crafts, with the former residence of Han-dynasty scholar Jia Yi along the way.
sights.hours: Open all day; shops ~10:00 AM–10:00 PM.

sights.name: Pozi Street and Huogongdian
sights.note: The city's classic snack street, home to the century-old Huogongdian (Fire Palace) restaurant: the place to try stinky tofu, sugar-oil cakes and spicy Hunan small plates.
sights.hours: Stalls and restaurants open from late morning to late night.

sights.name: Du Fu River Pavilion
sights.note: A tall riverside pavilion commemorating the Tang poet Du Fu, who spent his last years in Changsha; the river promenade around it faces Orange Isle and Mount Yuelu and is lit up at night.
sights.hours: Riverside open all day; pavilion interior roughly daytime hours, free.

sights.name: Hunan First Normal University (Old Campus)
sights.note: The rebuilt teacher-training school where the young Mao Zedong studied and later taught, with classrooms and dormitories laid out as they were in the 1910s.
sights.hours: Roughly 9:00 AM–5:00 PM; free (passport may be checked).

railStations.name: Changsha South Railway Station
railStations.note: Changsha's main high-speed rail hub, ~10 km south-east of the centre: G-trains to Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Wuhan, Beijing, Shanghai, Guilin and Kunming. Metro Lines 2 (to Wuyi Square in ~25 min) and 4 stop here, and the Maglev Express runs to the airport.

railStations.name: Changsha Railway Station
railStations.note: The older central station at the east end of Wuyi Avenue: conventional and intercity trains (including Changsha–Zhuzhou–Xiangtan intercity) and some high-speed services. Metro Lines 2 and 3 stop underneath; Wuyi Square is 3 stops west on Line 2.
railStations.hours: Trains from ~5:30 AM to after midnight to individual timetables; metro ~6:30 AM–~11:00 PM.

airports.name: Changsha Huanghua International Airport
airports.transitNote: About 25 km east of the centre. Metro Line 6 (on the subway map) runs from the T1 & T2 station across the city, with a change to Line 2 for Wuyi Square (~50–60 min, ~¥7). The Maglev Express (also on the map, separate ¥20 fare) runs to Changsha South Station in ~20 min. Taxis take ~40–60 min (~¥100–130).
airports.hours: Line 6 ~6:30 AM–~11:00 PM; Maglev first train ~7:00 AM, last ~10:30 PM.
